title: A Comparative Study Between Arachidonic Acid Treatment and Photobiomodulation Therapy on Bone Remodeling In-Vitro
content: Background: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of arachidonic acid (AA) and photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT), individually and in combination, on osteoclast and osteoblast activity in-vitro. Methods: Cells were treated with 40 µM AA, 14s of PBMT, or their combination. Untreated cells served as controls. Osteoclast differentiation was assessed using TRAP staining, while migration was evaluated using a transwell assay. Real time PCR assessed osteoclast activity genes such as NFATc1, TRAP, Cat-k, TGF-β, and MMP-9. Osteoblast function was assessed by ALP activity and mRNA expression of RUNX2, ALP, and OCN. The RANKL/OPG ratio was measured using ELISA. Results: PBMT and combined AA+PBMT treatment significantly enhanced cell migration. AA treatment upregulated osteoclastogenic markers and downregulated osteoblast-associated markers and ALP activity. In contrast, PBMT upregulated both osteoclastogenic and osteoblastogenic markers, along with increased ALP activity. The combined AA+PBMT treatment demonstrated enhanced osteoclastogenic activity, but reduced osteoblast-associated markers compared to controls. Additionally, AA and AA+PBMT increased the RANKL/OPG ratio, whereas PBMT decreased their ratio. Conclusions: AA and AA+PBMT treatment potentially favored osteoclastogenesis while PBMT exerted a dual modulatory effect on both osteoclast and osteoblast functions. The findings suggest the applicability of AA and PBMT as adjunctive interventions for bone remodeling.
